content.user_title: Optimize AI Prompts With Prompt Architect
content.value_statement: Weak prompts create inconsistent AI outputs and slow review cycles. This skill provides a structured process for improving prompts, testing them, and documenting changes.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes prompts against system context, role, task, constraints, format, examples, and quality criteria.
Identifies prompt anti-patterns such as vague wording, missing context, missing output format, and conflicting instructions.
Reorganizes prompts into a clear structure with role, scope, constraints, output format, and success criteria.
Adds prompt engineering techniques including chain-of-thought framing, self-consistency, ReAct, few-shot examples, and constraint framing.
Defines A/B test cases, scoring metrics, success rates, and consistency checks for prompt validation.
Produces final prompt, optimization report, test results, and reusable prompt library entry outputs.
limitations: It provides a workflow and templates, not guaranteed prompt performance improvements.
Validation requires representative test cases and external execution by the user or their tooling.
Some examples reference claude-flow commands that users must review before running.
It is focused on prompt design and does not replace domain expert review.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent System Prompts
use_cases.description: Refine role, constraints, tools, and output expectations for specialized AI agents.

use_cases.title: Standardize Prompt Reviews
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist to find missing context, vague instructions, and weak quality criteria.

use_cases.title: Build Tested Prompt Libraries
use_cases.description: Create reusable prompts with examples, validation cases, performance metrics, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this prompt for missing context, unclear instructions, weak constraints, missing output format, and absent success criteria: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this prompt using sections for system context, role, task, constraints, output format, examples, and quality criteria: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create typical, edge case, and stress test cases for this prompt. Include scoring criteria and expected response qualities: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Run Iterative Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the original prompt and latest prompt against test results. Diagnose failures, propose refinements, and produce the final prompt with a change summary.

output_examples.input: A vague support assistant prompt with no escalation rules or output format.
output_examples.output: A structured support prompt with role, customer context, escalation rules, response format, quality criteria, and three validation cases.

output_examples.input: A coding agent prompt that gives inconsistent pull request reviews.
output_examples.output: A revised review prompt with severity ordering, file reference requirements, test expectations, and examples of acceptable findings.

output_examples.input: A summarization prompt that misses key risks in long documents.
output_examples.output: An optimized prompt with scope limits, evidence requirements, risk categories, concise output rules, and a regression test plan.

best_practices: Start with a clear target task, audience, constraints, and output format before adding advanced techniques.
Validate prompt changes against realistic examples, edge cases, and failure cases before adopting them.
Document why each change was made so future reviewers can maintain the prompt safely.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize prompts only by adding length without improving structure or test coverage.
Do not rely on claimed percentage improvements without measured test results.
Do not run included shell examples before reviewing the commands and inputs.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It optimizes prompts for AI systems by improving structure, clarity, constraints, examples, and validation criteria.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The framework is model-agnostic and the metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.

faq.question: Does it automatically prove a prompt is better?
faq.answer: No. It provides test and metric templates, but users must run validation with realistic cases.

faq.question: Can it create new prompts from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can build prompts from a defined use case, role, constraints, output format, and examples.

faq.question: What outputs should I expect?
faq.answer: Expected outputs include a final optimized prompt, an optimization report, A/B test results, and a library entry.

faq.question: Are the command examples required?
faq.answer: No. The command examples are optional workflow integrations and should be reviewed before use.
